2607.11400.title: Cross-Architecture LLM Ensembles, Feature-Based Reranking and Retrieval-Augmented Prompting for Legal Information Processing
2607.11400.paper_summary: Legal information processing spans retrieval, entailment and judgment prediction problems, requiring text matching, reasoning and robust generalisation with limited supervision. We report Team DU's participation in all five tasks of COLIEE 2026, using open-weight systems for legal case retrieval, case entailment, statute retrieval and entailment, and legal judgment prediction. For Tasks 3 and 4, all models predate the 15 July 2025 cutoff required by the rules. For Task 4 (statute entailment), a cross-architecture ensemble of nine models from three families achieves 96.3% accuracy, placing first among 33 submissions from 11 teams. For the Pilot Task (tort prediction and rationale extraction), a multi-view system combining five claim-level models and refining the verdict using features derived from the claim predictions achieves 73.1% TP accuracy and 68.2% RE F1 as an unofficial submission, scoring above all official entries on TP and matching the highest on RE. For Task 2 (legal case entailment), changing only the prompt from single- to multi-selection raises F1 from 0.343 to 0.555 in post-competition evaluation on released gold labels, exceeding the best official submission (F1 = 0.490). For Task 3 (statute retrieval and entailment), replacing the entailment model with Qwen3-235B and a structured legal reasoning prompt raises accuracy from 79.3% to 91.5% in post-competition analysis. For Task 1 (legal case retrieval), a learning-to-rank system combining lexical and semantic retrieval with structural, citation authority, and temporal features (34 in total) achieves F1 = 0.314 (rank 11 of 54 submissions from 22 teams). Overall, legal information processing benefits from different inductive biases across tasks, with cross-architecture ensembling, feature-based reranking and retrieval-augmented prompting each proving most effective in different settings.
2607.11400.paper_summary_zh: 法律信息處理涵蓋檢索、推理和判決預測問題，需要文本匹配、推理和在有限監督下的穩健泛化。<lb/>我們報告了DU團隊參加2026年COLIEE所有五個任務的情況，使用開放權重系統進行法律案件檢索、案件推理、法規檢索和推理，以及法律判決預測。<lb/>對於任務3和4，所有模型均早於規則要求的2025年7月15日截止日期。<lb/>在任務4（法規推理）中，來自三個家族的九個模型的跨架構集成達到96.3%的準確率，在11個團隊的33個提交中名列第一。<lb/>在試點任務（侵權預測和理由提取）中，結合五個索賠級別模型的多視角系統，並使用從索賠預測中派生的特徵來細化判決，達到73.1%的TP準確率和68.2%的RE F1，作為非官方提交，TP得分高於所有官方條目，RE得分與最高的條目相匹配。<lb/>在任務2（法律案件推理）中，僅更改提示從單選到多選，F1在競賽後評估中從0.343提高到0.555，超過最佳官方提交（F1 = 0.490）。<lb/>在任務3（法規檢索和推理）中，用Qwen3-235B替換推理模型並使用結構化法律推理提示，準確率在競賽後分析中從79.3%提高到91.5%。<lb/>在任務1（法律案件檢索）中，結合詞彙和語義檢索與結構、引用權威和時間特徵（共34個）的學習排序系統達到F1 = 0.314（在22個團隊的54個提交中排名第11）。<lb/>總體而言，法律信息處理受益於不同任務之間的歧義偏見，跨架構集成、基於特徵的重新排序和檢索增強提示在不同設置中各自證明最有效。
